parts.transcript: Part 3: Frances and Sam discuss a report using business analysis tools. PEST didn't fit their company (21=C); Drill Down took too long/painstaking (22=D); PMI is easy to use, no training needed (23=E); Pareto saves time and effort - 20% of problems give 80% of benefits (24=A); SWOT suits companies of all sizes (25=G). Their case company: best strength is its experienced employees who previously worked for distributors (26=B); they overlooked setting up an overseas/offshore office (27=B); a threat is new legislation/environmental policy (28=C); Sam learned the gap between theory and the real world (29=C); the tutor suggests they give a final determination on whether the company should go ahead (30=A).
parts.instruction: You will hear two students called Frances and Sam talking to their tutor about a report on business analysis tools.

parts.title: Employment Survey on Graduates
parts.transcript: Part 4: a researcher presents an Employment Survey on Graduates of the Business Management (31) course. Two methods: email questionnaires and phone interviews (32). Findings: 32% went on to acquire another qualification (33); only 4% unemployed; most work in the public sector (34); the majority are happy with their salary/career development (35). Useful skills from the course: working as a team member (36), personal organisation, problem-solving ability (37). Least valuable: presentations - lack of training (38); advice/work on essay writing - unnecessary (39); and not enough advice on finding a job (40).
